title: pydantic dataclass interop, streaming iterators, retry semantics, and cookbook examples
creator: Priya Singh
description: Unify typed response parsing in the Python SDK: provide ergonomic helpers to interoperate between dataclasses and Pydantic models, offer streaming iterators that yield typed partial/complete objects, and standardize retry semantics for both full and streamed responses. Deliver a cookbook with concrete examples (sync/async, streaming, retry hooks, migration patterns). Keep the opt-in nature of helpers to preserve backwards compatibility and target low-latency code paths for production usage.
acceptance_criteria: Pydantic and dataclass models can be used interchangeably in response parsing via provided adapters
Streaming endpoints expose an async iterator that yields typed partial objects as they arrive and supports backpressure
Retry behavior for transient network or parse errors is documented and configurable at call-site and at client level
A cookbook with at least five examples (sync parsing, async parsing, streaming typed iterator, retry-on-parse, migration guide) is published in SDK docs
Unit and integration tests cover parsing edge cases and ensure <90ms median overhead compared to current untyped parsing path
technical_notes: Primary approaches considered: dataclass-first (fast dataclass parsing + optional pydantic validation) vs pydantic-first (rich validation, heavier runtime)
Decision: dataclass-first for low-latency paths; provide pydantic wrappers for strict schema enforcement and developer ergonomics
Streaming model: implement AsyncTypedIterator[T] that yields dataclass instances as incremental chunks are parsed; provide hooks for partial validation and user callbacks
Retry semantics: separate network-level idempotent retries from parse-level retries; allow user-defined parse_retry hook to re-request from a cursor when safe
Compatibility: helpers are opt-in via client.parse_as(MyModel) or client.stream_as(MyModel); default client.generate() remains unchanged
implementation_plan: Add dataclass parser module: sdk/typing/dataclass_adapter.py with from_dict/try_from_bytes helpers
Add optional pydantic integration: sdk/typing/pydantic_adapter.py exposing validate_model and as_dataclass helpers
Introduce TypedResponse and AsyncTypedIterator classes under sdk/typing/response.py with consistent API for sync/async consumers
Expose client.parse_response(model=..., streaming=False) and client.stream_response(model=..., streaming=True) API overloads; keep legacy generate() for compatibility
Create cookbook examples under examples/python/typed_streaming/ and new docs page docs/cookbook/typed-streaming.md
Add tests and microbenchmarks under tests/sdk/typing/ and benchmarks/typing to validate performance targets
testing_plan: Unit tests for dataclass <-> dict conversion, optional pydantic validation, and missing/extra fields handling
Integration tests with mocked streaming JSON lines and chunk boundary fragmentation to ensure incremental parsing behaves correctly
Simulate transient parse and network errors to validate retry hooks and idempotency rules for stream vs non-stream calls
Performance benchmarks comparing typed helpers vs current untyped parsing on representative payloads
